bulgaria.intro:
Bulgaria is a Balkan country with a long Black Sea coast, mountain ranges, ancient towns and generous, affordable food. Its cooking mixes Balkan, Turkish and Greek influences.

This page explains what Bulgaria is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
Bulgaria is known for the Rila and Pirin mountains, the Rose Valley, Black Sea beaches and old towns such as Plovdiv and Veliko Tarnovo. It is one of the oldest countries in Europe, and its monasteries and Thracian tombs reflect a deep history.

The country is also known for yogurt, wine and folk music.

Shopska salad, with tomato, cucumber, peppers and white sirene cheese, is the national starter. Banitsa, a flaky cheese pastry, is eaten at breakfast, and tarator, a cold yogurt and cucumber soup, is a summer favorite. Kebapche and kyufte grilled meats, sarma, stuffed cabbage leaves, and moussaka are common mains.

Bulgarian yogurt is world famous, and rakia, a fruit brandy, and local wines accompany meals.

Sofia offers the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and mountain views, Plovdiv has a Roman theater and an old town, and Veliko Tarnovo has a hilltop fortress. Rila Monastery and Bansko are mountain highlights, and Nessebar and Sozopol are Black Sea gems.

The Rose Valley blooms in late spring.

sections.h2: What Blagoevgrad Province is known for
sections.body:
The province is known for Bansko, a top ski resort, the Pirin and Rila mountains, Rila Monastery and Melnik, the smallest town in Bulgaria and a wine center. It has natural hot springs and old stone houses.

The highland climate brings snow in winter and cool summers.

Mountain restaurants serve grilled meat, kapama, a slow cooked stew, and banitsa. Bansko is known for its traditional mehanas with hearty dishes in clay pots. Melnik is known for its red wine, made from the local Shiroka Melnishka grape.

Cheese, honey and herbal tea are local products.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Blagoevgrad Province
sections.body:
Bansko offers skiing and summer hiking, Rila Monastery is a spiritual and architectural landmark, and the Seven Rila Lakes are a popular hike. Melnik has sandstone pyramids and wine cellars, and Rozhen Monastery is nearby.

Sandanski has hot springs.

bulgaria/blagoevgrad-province/bansko.intro:
Bansko is a mountain town at the foot of Pirin, known as Bulgaria's leading ski resort and for its stone houses and traditional taverns.

sections.body:
The town is known for its ski area, with a gondola from the edge of town, for its old town with stone houses and for the Bansko Jazz Festival in summer. Many visitors come for hiking in Pirin National Park.

The old town has more than a hundred mehanas.

Traditional mehanas serve grilled meats, kapama, kavarma, a clay pot stew, sausages and banitsa, usually with live folk music. Local specialties include Bansko sausage, called Banski starets, and potato dishes. Homemade rakia and local wine are served.

After skiing, cafes serve hot chocolate and mulled wine.

The gondola up to the ski area, the Holy Trinity Church, the Velyanov House and the Pirin National Park are highlights. In summer, hiking to Vihren and the Banderitsa valley is popular.

Rila Monastery and Melnik are day trips.

bulgaria/blagoevgrad-province/melnik.intro:
Melnik is the smallest town in Bulgaria, in a valley of sand pyramids, with houses tucked into the hillside and wine cellars cut into rock.

This page explains what Melnik is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The town is known for its red wine, its old Revival houses and its dramatic sandstone formations. Winemaking here goes back centuries, and many families still keep cellars.

The town is quiet, with only a few streets, and the setting is memorable.

Wine is the main attraction, especially the local Shiroka Melnishka grape and Melnik 55. Restaurants serve grilled meats, kapama, cheese, local bread and Shopska salad. Honey and herbs from the hills are sold.

Food is hearty and simple, ideal with wine.

Visit the Kordopulov House, the wine cellars and the walk to the Rozhen Monastery. The sand pyramids make good photo walks. Rupite, a nearby volcanic area, is also visited.

Sandanski and Bansko are within a short drive.

The province is known for Sunny Beach, the largest beach resort in the country, for Nessebar, a World Heritage old town on a peninsula, and for Sozopol and Burgas. Wetlands attract migrating birds.

The coast is lively in summer.

Seafood is the highlight, including fried sprats, mussels, grilled fish and shopska salad. Black Sea fish soup, rakia and local wine complement meals. Sweets include baklava and ice cream, and banitsa is a breakfast staple.

Coastal restaurants offer sea views. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Burgas Province
sections.body:
Nessebar has churches and a cobbled old town, Sozopol is a charming fishing town, and Sunny Beach is for beaches and nightlife. Burgas has a sea garden and lakes with birds.

The Strandzha mountains offer forests and villages.

The city is known for the Sea Garden, a wide park on the cliff, the beach, the harbor and nearby lakes that attract birds. It hosts music and arts events in summer, including a large sand sculpture festival.

It is a base for trips to Sozopol and Nessebar.

Seafood is central, with grilled fish, fried sprats, mussels and Black Sea fish soup. Try shopska salad, banitsa and sweets. Restaurants by the sea garden and harbor offer views.

Street stalls sell corn, ice cream and sunflower seeds. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

The Sea Garden, the Burgas Lakes, the St. Cyril and Methodius Cathedral and the harbor are the highlights. Poda Nature Reserve is good for birdwatching.

Sozopol and Nessebar are about 40 minutes away.

Nessebar is a walled peninsula town on the Black Sea, with a World Heritage old town of churches, wooden houses and cobbled lanes.

This page explains what Nessebar is known for, what to eat and where to go, and helps you use the listings to compare ratings, photos and locations before you choose a table.

sections.body:
The town is known for its ruined Byzantine churches, its windmill, its charming wooden houses and its sunset views over the sea. History here goes back three thousand years.

The old town is compact and pedestrian, linked to the new town by a narrow causeway.

Seafood is the star, with fried sprats, mussels, grilled fish and fish soup. Shopska salad, grilled meat and banitsa are on every menu, and many restaurants are on terraces over the water. Local wine and rakia are served.

Ice cream and sweet pastries are sold along the lanes.

The old town churches such as St. Stephen and Christ Pantokrator, the archaeological museum and the old fortress gate are highlights. The harbor and the windmill make good photo spots.

Sunny Beach is a few minutes away.

The resort is close to Nessebar's old town.

Restaurants offer a wide mix, with Bulgarian grills, seafood, pizza and international food. Try shopska salad, kebapche, grilled fish and banitsa. Many places have set meals and menus in several languages.

The province is known for Plovdiv, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe, and for the Rhodope mountains with Bachkovo Monastery. Wine and vegetables thrive in the fertile Thracian plain.

The region is rich in folk traditions.

Look for grilled meats, Shopska salad, banitsa and stews. Local wines, especially Mavrud, a red grape, are well known. Plovdiv has a vibrant cafe and street food scene, and the Rhodopes are known for lamb, potatoes and cheese.

Fresh fruit and vegetable markets are excellent. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Plovdiv Province
sections.body:
Plovdiv's old town and Roman theater, the Bachkovo Monastery, the Asen's Fortress and the Rhodope villages are highlights. Karlovo is known for its rose oil history, and Hisarya has hot springs.

The wine route around Brestovitsa is popular.

The pedestrian main street is lively in the evening.

Try grilled meats, kebapche, Shopska salad, banitsa and stews, along with Mavrud red wine from nearby vineyards. Kapana has modern places with craft beer and creative menus. Sweet pastries and baklava are widely available.

Street food includes gyros and fresh bread. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

The Ancient Theater, the Roman Stadium, the Old Town, the Hill of the Liberators and Kapana are highlights. Bachkovo Monastery is a short drive, and the Rhodopes are close.

The Singing Fountains are a summer evening attraction.

sections.h2: What Sofia City is known for
sections.body:
The area is known for the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Vitosha mountain and a growing creative scene. It is one of the oldest capitals in Europe, with Roman, Ottoman and Soviet layers.

Its parks and cafes give it a relaxed feel.

Sofia's restaurants serve traditional dishes such as Shopska salad, kapama, banitsa and kebapche, along with modern European and Asian food. Cafes, bakeries and bars are everywhere, and the city has a strong coffee culture.

Wine and craft beer are popular. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.body:

The sea garden and the beaches draw crowds in summer.

Seafood is the specialty, with fried sprats, fish soup, mussels and grilled fish. Local white wines and craft beers are popular. Dishes such as Shopska salad and banitsa are on every menu.

Cafes serve sweets and ice cream along the promenade. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Varna Province

Varna has a sea garden, a Roman bath and the Archaeological Museum with the world's oldest gold. Golden Sands has beaches, and Balchik has a palace and botanical garden.

Aladzha Monastery is a rock hewn site in a forest.

sections.h2: What Veliko Tarnovo is known for
sections.body:
The province is known for Veliko Tarnovo, the capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire, with its fortress on a hill above a looping river. Nearby are Arbanasi, with stone houses, and the Transfiguration Monastery.

The area is quiet, scenic and full of history.

Local food is hearty, with grilled meats, banitsa, stews and lamb. Restaurants serve Shopska salad, kapama and kavarma, and cafes serve coffee and pastries. Local wines and rakia are common.

Traditional dishes are often cooked in clay pots. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Veliko Tarnovo
sections.body:
Tsarevets Fortress, the Asenevtsi monument, Arbanasi village and the Transfiguration Monastery are highlights. The Emen canyon and the Ivanovo rock churches are close.

The Sound and Light show at the fortress is a summer evening event.

A sound and light show lights up the fortress at night.

Look for kapama, kavarma, grilled meats, banitsa and Shopska salad. Restaurants with terraces offer views over the river. Cafes serve strong coffee and sweet pastries, and craft workshops sell local honey and rakia.

The local wines are good value. Portions are generous and prices are friendly, so it is easy to try several dishes, and many places bring a complimentary bread basket or a small plate of cheese to the table.

sections.h2: Places to visit in Veliko Tarnovo

Tsarevets Fortress, the Asenevtsi monument and Samovodska Charshia are the main sights. The Arbanasi village and the Transfiguration Monastery are short rides, and the Emen canyon offers trails.
